subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable umask / file permissions for agent-created user-facing files

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in user-output file permission policy, and if so should it be scoped to tools.fs user artifacts or cover broader shared-host permission categories?
rationale: The requested fix changes local filesystem access boundaries and adds config surface; automation cannot choose the acceptable security model or upgrade behavior for shared-host deployments.

options.title: Add narrow tools artifact policy
options.body: Add an opt-in tools-scoped user-output policy with explicit private-state exclusions and tests across the supported agent write paths.

options.title: Reject a core permission knob
options.body: Keep OpenClaw defaults restrictive and tell operators to solve shared-host permissions with host ACLs, container users, or deployment docs.

options.title: Design broader shared-host policy
options.body: Treat user artifacts and private-state ACL compatibility as one larger security design before accepting implementation PRs.

recommendation.title: Add narrow tools artifact policy
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in tools-scoped user-output policy with explicit private-state exclusions and tests across the supported agent write paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely decision spans config schema/types and the central agent tool filesystem path where recent ownership evidence points most strongly to vincentkoc.
